newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Brent crude still faces long march south.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Brent crude still faces long march south.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+ IPE Brent set to move lower again after range trading of recent sessions fizzles out, technical analysts and traders said
+ Longterm downtrend seen set to resume pressure with a consistent return over $18.00 a barrel looking increasingly distant.
IPE Brent crude oil futures looked set to resume the march south to fresh calendar year lows this week, technical analysts said on Thursday.
A spate of range-trading in early April seemed ready to fizzle out with the long term crude downtrend from January still holding sway.
"Brent closed near the low yesterday and is looking very bearish," said Steve Kwan of MMS in London.
"Recently there has been bottoming out on momentum indicators but it has failed to move to the upside, which is not a very good sign at all," Kwan added.

June Brent closed 33 cents down at $17.81 a barrel on Wednesday, just three cents off the session low. But the echo of the $17.80 close from April 10 did not suggest the formation of reliable support, some chartists said.
Kwan still kept an eye on the trading gap left at $18.62-18.77 from the April 2-3 sessions, but with June looking unsustainable above $18.00 he saw that as a receeding prospect.
That, and subsequent range trading, suggested to him a bearish flag pattern, which, with the gap still open, indicated a potential eventual drop to the $17.10 mark.
Mees Pierson analyst Nicholas Wilson was also bearish.
"(Short term) we will dribble down a bit but the downtrend is maturing and the technicals are all pointing south," Wilson said.

He too saw the recent range, which he identified as centred on $17.90-$18.50, as looking tired and pointed to a downside target of $17.47 to be achieved by the end of the week, based on this year's downtrend.
"Ultimately -- in a month to six weeks -- I'm looking at $16.10, an old support from August of last year," Wilson added.
Analysts saw IPE gas oil futures also in thrall to the greater downtrend.

May gas oil settled $2.50 lower at $162.75 a tonne on Wednesday. The $162.25 level respresents a band of support from early April, broken by what some termed a bear trap dip to $159.75 a few sessions ago.
Wilson looked for a short term target of $155.00 and a longer term goal of $149.00.
